- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast growth to 1–2% per day post-spike.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–6% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75 and true outcome drops below 70, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag true price movements; increase forecast sensitivity to recent 7-day history.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per event to account for supply pressure.
